text:
Four hundred and forty billion euros.

That's how much households in Europe hold in American tech stocks, according to economists at the European Central Bank.

And here's the part that got my attention: most of them don't even know it.

And it's not just households. According to the same analysis, insurance companies and pension funds have a similar exposure to big tech. So even your pension may be making the same bet.

Because they never bought Nvidia. They never bought Microsoft. They bought a world ETF.

One fund. Thousands of companies. Safe, simple, diversified. At least, that's the idea.

Now look at what happened in September. In the middle of the month, the Nasdaq one hundred lost more than six hundred billion dollars in two days.

Then, within a week, it bounced back by trillions. Fear, then greed, then fear again.

Valuations in the US are at the second highest level in more than a hundred and fifty years.

The only time they were higher? December 1999.

So I did what this channel does. I took real euro data, going back to 1999, and I replayed the dot-com crash on the portfolio most Europeans own today.

You'll see how long it took to get your money back, what the dollar did to euro investors, which safer alternatives actually helped, and which ones barely made a difference.

And at the end, I'll show you one number that matters more than any crash.

This is The AI Bubble in Europe.
